newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end mostly up in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end mostly up in thin trade.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher, except for spot September, due to light technical buying from local investors, traders said on Friday.

Spot September closed shed 110 yen to end at 14,580 yen per tonne. Other contracts ranged from 40 to 70 yen higher, with the benchmark July 1998 contract rising 50 yen to end at 13,790 yen. Estimated volume was 24,980 lots.
The CBOT corn market's losses overnight triggered light selling during the morning session, but technical buying from local investors emerged by early afternoon trade, traders said.
The spot September corn contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was trading at $2.43 per bushel at 0810 GMT, against $2.43-1/2 at Thursday's close.
The spot August CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.50-1/2 per bushel at 0810 GMT, against $7.52 at Thursday's close.
